background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.
A later successful build replaces the earlier one; do not assume automatic best-candidate
selection or rollback. Do not emit an unexecutable final revision after executions run out.

Reference inventory and parameterization:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps, and
uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from this input, not calibration.
Also record several reliable shared projection anchors distributed across the image:
long edges, intersections, repeated-size relationships, and major foreground cropping.
Distinguish observed edges from inferred geometry. Avoid false precision in uncertain bounds.
Map inventory items to named SceneAct assets with meaningful child parts. A valid hierarchy
verifies only emitted parts; it does not establish photographic completeness.
Do not invent hidden detail to fill uncertainty or discard a visible part solely for being small.

Keep camera parameters, layout, whole-object dimensions, component proportions and finishes
separately editable. Build reusable assemblies in a consistent local frame before placing
instances. Use explicit pivots for transforms when the default AABB center is inappropriate.
Do not rely on an empty group's origin being its geometry center. Preserve group membership,
semantic children and support relations through revisions and complexity reductions.

Fit projection, silhouette and coverage before microstructure. Use a compact complete first
scene, including all major visible content. Estimate camera pose and focal length jointly
from multiple anchors instead of fitting a single salient object. Check foreground cropping,
relative projected sizes, convergence and occlusion order together. Repeated objects provide
constraints but need not have identical visible silhouettes or perfectly regular placement.
For composite objects, estimate the overall silhouette, internal occupied space and gaps,
component aspect ratios, and visible underside or opening before adding repeated details.
An outer bounding box does not establish correct shape or internal coverage. Uniform size
and camera-ray distance changes cannot directly repair an intrinsic component aspect ratio.
A projected AABB is only a coarse correspondence aid, not a visible silhouette mask. Extreme
bounds may arise from near-plane crossings or behind-camera geometry; inspect the render
before treating them as evidence that geometry must be resized or deleted.

Rendered review and uncertainty:
Use the first execution for a complete scene, leaving another available for correction.
After a render, compare against the original reference at full-image and local scales:
shared anchors and cropping; salient silhouettes, component proportions and gaps; visible
coverage and occlusion; broad brightness and material regions; then fine details.
Separate image evidence from priors about what the depicted objects usually look like.
Record a brief revision rationale in program comments: observed discrepancy, competing
explanations, selected parameter family, expected visible effect, and uncertainty.

When many independently placed anchors share an error, investigate camera/framing. When
anchors agree but one assembly differs, investigate its placement or shape. Neither pattern
proves a unique cause. Do not mandate a camera correction before every local correction, or
interpret every local error as geometry. Keep camera pitch, focal length, object distance,
whole-object scale and component proportions conceptually distinct. Avoid simultaneous,
unexplained changes to all of them. Prefer a small coherent correction supported by several
visible comparisons; retain already matching objects and uncertain alternatives.

If controlled observations or an executable module decision are supplied, use their actual
reported result rather than an earlier preferred hypothesis. An unresolved decision remains
unresolved: do not force a winning module from the sign of one score or nearly tied weights.
Measured interventions report appearance sensitivity under the tested conditions, not true
3D accuracy. A beneficial local scale response can compensate for camera or shape errors;
a harmful focal change rejects neither all camera explanations nor the opposite direction.
Do not extrapolate one tested magnitude or direction into a universal correction rule.
Only compare baseline-relative interventions when their baseline, reference region, metric
and rendering conditions are compatible. Preserve the reference region across comparisons;
do not move it with the edited object to improve a score. Inspect full-image and regional
changes separately when available, since a combined scalar can conceal damage elsewhere.
Predicted intervals are forecasts, not measurements or calibrated confidence intervals.
A forecast miss alone does not establish causal falsity. Untested interventions remain unknown.

confounds its similarity score; it does not justify removing the rest of the reconstruction.

material palette instead of distinct random materials for tiny primitives.
If execution times out without an image, report failed completion and leave the bottleneck

If execution fails, use its actual traceback. A failed execution without an image supplies

from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math
import random

# Reference inventory (normalized image bounds, approximate):
# Room: pale cream back wall (.12,.38)-(.53,.60); right wall (.52,.00)-(1,.78).
# Dark carpet covers lower .40 of image, with right wall black baseboard.
# Large right-wall whiteboard (.59,.26)-(.91,.58), aluminum border and two panels.
# Left luminous windows (.00,.33)-(.12,.67), cropped by image left.
# Suspended ceiling fills upper left; rectangular tiles, lights and missing edge tiles.
# Hanging US flag (.45,.33)-(.51,.43), diagonal pole toward right wall.
# Back wall vent, open electrical enclosure, dangling cover and small wall plates.
# Floor debris: gray torn panels left/center, yellow layered sheets at lower right,
# and long aluminum ceiling rails cropped by the bottom-right edge.
# Shared observed anchors: back floor corners near (.12,.61),(.52,.59);
# back ceiling line near y=.38; right board verticals and receding top/bottom edges;
# right baseboard runs from (.52,.59) to (1,.78). Hidden room extent is inferred.
# Editable parameter families: camera, room dimensions, board, ceiling grid, debris.
# Expanded primitive estimate: about 200 boxes/rods, plus 13 flag stripes.
# No rendered feedback is available at this initial build.

random.seed(12)
scene = Scene(name="Vacant classroom")
W, D, H = 4.65, 7.6, 2.95
cream = (.69,.675,.60)
ceiling_col = (.65,.67,.66)
metal = (.48,.52,.52)
dark = (.055,.065,.058)

def asset(name):
    a = Asset(name=name)
    scene.include(name, a)
    return a

def bx(parent, name, size, center, color, rotation=None):
    obj = box(size=size, center=center, color=color)
    if rotation:
        obj.turn(euler=rotation, pivot=center)
    parent.include(name, obj)
    return obj

def rd(parent, name, a, b, radius, color):
    obj = rod(radius=radius, start=a, end=b, color=color)
    parent.include(name, obj)
    return obj

architecture = asset("Room shell")
bx(architecture,"Carpet",(W+1,D+3,.12),(W/2,D/2-.8,-.07),(.16,.17,.145))
bx(architecture,"Right plaster wall",(.12,D+2,H),(W+.06,D/2-.7,H/2),cream)
bx(architecture,"Back plaster wall",(W,.12,H),(W/2,D+.06,H/2),cream)
bx(architecture,"Left wall",(.12,D,H),(-.06,D/2,H/2),(.73,.74,.70))
bx(architecture,"Right black skirting",(.035,D+.5,.115),(W-.025,D/2-.25,.057),dark)
bx(architecture,"Back black skirting",(W,.035,.115),(W/2,D-.025,.057),dark)
bx(architecture,"Left black skirting",(.035,D,.1),(.02,D/2,.05),dark)

windows = asset("Left translucent window wall")
for j in range(4):
    yy = .78+j*1.38
    bx(windows,"Opaque glowing pane %d"%j,(.025,1.34,2.56),(.022,yy,1.49),(.86,.90,.90))
    bx(windows,"Window mullion %d"%j,(.052,.022,2.65),(.043,yy+.68,1.48),(.70,.75,.75))
for zz in (.2,1.52,2.77):
    bx(windows,"Window horizontal rail %.2f"%zz,(.055,5.65,.024),(.05,2.82,zz),(.72,.77,.77))

ceiling = asset("Suspended acoustic ceiling")
bx(ceiling,"Dark plenum",(W+.2,D+.5,.055),(W/2,D/2,H+.19),(.095,.115,.11))
sx, sy = .79, 1.22
for i in range(6):
    for j in range(7):
        xx, yy = (i+.5)*sx, (j+.5)*sy-.6
        if xx>W or yy>D:
            continue
        # Missing tiles along the left side expose a dark ceiling cavity.
        if i==0 and j in (0,1,3,4):
            continue
        c=ceiling_col
        if (i,j) in ((1,2),(1,3),(2,5)):
            c=(.77,.79,.77)
        bx(ceiling,"Acoustic tile %d %d"%(i,j),(sx-.022,sy-.022,.025),(xx,yy,H),c)
for i in range(7):
    xx=i*sx
    if xx<=W:
        bx(ceiling,"Long grid runner %d"%i,(.018,D+.8,.025),(xx,D/2-.3,H-.016),(.55,.59,.58))
for j in range(8):
    yy=j*sy-.6
    if yy<=D:
        bx(ceiling,"Cross grid runner %d"%j,(W,.018,.025),(W/2,yy,H-.016),(.56,.60,.59))
for j in (2,4):
    bx(ceiling,"Recessed fluorescent frame %d"%j,(.68,1.12,.025),(1.185,j*sy+.01,H-.033),(.52,.56,.56))
    bx(ceiling,"Fluorescent diffuser %d"%j,(.62,1.06,.012),(1.185,j*sy+.01,H-.051),(.78,.82,.81))
rd(ceiling,"Loose ceiling wire",(.18,4.8,H+.02),(.24,4.66,2.48),.008,(.12,.14,.14))

board = asset("Right wall whiteboard")
board_y, board_len = 4.95, 3.12
board_z, board_h = 1.77, 1.36
bx(board,"Board backing",(.035,board_len,board_h),(W-.045,board_y,board_z),(.68,.70,.68))
bx(board,"White writing surface",(.012,board_len-.065,board_h-.065),(W-.069,board_y,board_z),(.78,.80,.79))
for zz, nm in ((board_z-board_h/2,"Bottom frame"),(board_z+board_h/2,"Top frame")):
    bx(board,nm,(.052,board_len+.035,.025),(W-.08,board_y,zz),(.57,.61,.62))
for yy, nm in ((board_y-board_len/2,"Near end frame"),(board_y+board_len/2,"Far end frame")):
    bx(board,nm,(.052,.023,board_h+.03),(W-.08,yy,board_z),(.55,.59,.61))
bx(board,"Center divider",(.021,.012,board_h-.04),(W-.082,board_y+.28,board_z),(.63,.66,.65))
bx(board,"Narrow marker tray",(.085,board_len,.025),(W-.095,board_y,board_z-board_h/2-.025),(.54,.58,.58))
for yy in (board_y-board_len/2+.08,board_y+board_len/2-.08):
    bx(board,"Top mounting clip %.1f"%yy,(.027,.055,.08),(W-.08,yy,board_z+board_h/2+.025),(.47,.50,.49))

fixtures = asset("Back wall fixtures")
bx(fixtures,"Vent dark opening",(.91,.025,.37),(.93,D-.03,2.13),(.24,.29,.29))
for k in range(9):
    bx(fixtures,"Vent horizontal louver %d"%k,(.85,.028,.013),(.93,D-.051,1.98+k*.036),(.32,.37,.36))
bx(fixtures,"Electrical panel surround",(.28,.035,.41),(2.08,D-.035,1.89),(.49,.53,.51))
bx(fixtures,"Electrical panel black cavity",(.22,.016,.32),(2.08,D-.063,1.9),(.11,.14,.13))
for k in range(4):
    bx(fixtures,"Breaker %d"%k,(.06,.025,.037),(2.06+(k%2)*.075,D-.083,1.82+(k//2)*.10),(.47,.49,.45))
cover=bx(fixtures,"Loose hanging panel cover",(.43,.035,.34),(2.25,D-.13,1.58),(.43,.49,.47))
cover.turn(axis="+y",degrees=39,pivot=(2.25,D-.13,1.58))
for xx,zz in ((2.69,1.64),(2.88,1.69)):
    bx(fixtures,"Small wall plate %.2f"%xx,(.13,.02,.18),(xx,D-.035,zz),(.75,.75,.68))
    bx(fixtures,"Plate inset %.2f"%xx,(.05,.012,.045),(xx,D-.05,zz+.02),(.43,.46,.42))
bx(fixtures,"Right wall outlet",(.018,.085,.135),(W-.065,5.8,.50),(.64,.63,.53))

flag = asset("American flag and diagonal bracket")
rd(flag,"Flagpole",(W-.03,6.49,2.60),(3.23,6.68,2.97),.012,(.28,.29,.26))
# Hanging cloth is constructed in narrow vertical folds, with horizontal stripes.
flag_x, flag_y, flag_top = 3.25,6.64,2.94
fw, fh = .36,.76
for k in range(13):
    ztop=flag_top-k*fh/13
    col=(.56,.055,.055) if k%2==0 else (.83,.82,.73)
    for q in range(4):
        xx=flag_x+q*fw/4+fw/8
        yy=flag_y+.030*math.sin(q*2.1+k*.27)
        bx(flag,"Cloth stripe %d fold %d"%(k,q),(fw/4+.004,.014,fh/13+.002),(xx,yy,ztop-fh/26),col)
bx(flag,"Blue canton",(.185,.018,.36),(flag_x+.09,flag_y-.022,flag_top-.18),(.09,.14,.23))
for r in range(5):
    for c in range(4):
        bx(flag,"Small star %d %d"%(r,c),(.009,.006,.011),(flag_x+.025+c*.041,flag_y-.034,flag_top-.038-r*.064),(.81,.82,.75))

debris = asset("Scattered ceiling debris")
# Assemblies use explicit centers and pivots to retain editable whole-object placement.
def fragment(name, center, size, angle, color):
    p=Asset(name=name)
    debris.include(name,p)
    slab=bx(p,"Broken panel",size,center,color)
    slab.turn(axis="+z",degrees=angle,pivot=center)
    return p
fragment("Foreground torn panel",(.93,1.7,.025),(1.28,.56,.028),-12,(.32,.34,.29))
fragment("Foreground overlapping piece",(1.29,1.86,.047),(.90,.34,.022),17,(.37,.38,.32))
fragment("Left middle panel",(.42,3.28,.022),(.96,.38,.025),-8,(.36,.37,.31))
fragment("Back scattered panel",(1.36,4.86,.025),(1.12,.35,.026),9,(.28,.30,.25))
fragment("Small back panel",(1.08,5.02,.046),(.55,.26,.018),-19,(.42,.43,.36))
for k in range(13):
    xx=random.uniform(.4,2.0)
    yy=random.uniform(1.5,5.1)
    rd(debris,"Torn dark edging %d"%k,(xx,yy,.045),(xx+random.uniform(.15,.48),yy+random.uniform(-.2,.2),.047),.009,(.10,.13,.11))
for k in range(23):
    xx=random.uniform(.2,4.4)
    yy=random.uniform(1.1,6.8)
    s=random.uniform(.012,.045)
    bx(debris,"Small plaster chip %d"%k,(s,s*.65,.008),(xx,yy,.012),(.50,.49,.39))

yellow = asset("Collapsed yellow ceiling panels")
for k in range(4):
    ctr=(3.83-.09*k,2.65+.10*k,.075+.023*k)
    obj=bx(yellow,"Layered yellow sheet %d"%k,(1.24,.95,.028),ctr,(.59+.035*k,.45+.035*k,.15+.018*k))
    obj.turn(euler=(2, -4, -7),pivot=ctr)
# A raised, sloping front sheet gives the distinctive bent, broad yellow silhouette.
ctr=(4.00,2.49,.19)
obj=bx(yellow,"Bent raised yellow panel",(.92,1.10,.035),ctr,(.71,.56,.21))
obj.turn(euler=(-13,7,-7),pivot=ctr)
for k in range(4):
    rd(yellow,"Exposed layered edge %d"%k,(3.16,2.27+.05*k,.08+.022*k),(3.21,3.03+.05*k,.11+.022*k),.012,(.55,.44,.19))

rails = asset("Fallen metal ceiling runners")
rd(rails,"Long silver foreground rail",(3.94,1.85,.035),(4.79,-.70,.035),.024,(.59,.62,.59))
rd(rails,"Second silver foreground rail",(4.39,2.10,.03),(5.32,-.30,.03),.018,(.68,.69,.63))
rd(rails,"Left pale cross rail",(.74,2.99,.045),(2.17,2.69,.045),.017,(.57,.64,.64))
rd(rails,"Left rail dark flange",(.77,3.015,.027),(2.19,2.715,.027),.012,(.24,.29,.28))

realize(scene)

# Restrained procedural finishes retain the large observed tonal regions.
for obj in bpy.data.objects:
    if obj.type!='MESH' or not obj.data.materials:
        continue
    mat=obj.data.materials[0]
    mat.use_nodes=True
    bs=mat.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if bs:
        bs.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=.86

# Carpet variation is surface shading, not geometry.
for obj in bpy.data.objects:
    if obj.type=='MESH' and "Carpet" in obj.name and obj.data.materials:
        mat=obj.data.materials[0]
        nt=mat.node_tree
        bs=nt.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
        noise=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
        noise.inputs["Scale"].default_value=185
        noise.inputs["Detail"].default_value=2
        ramp=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=.20
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=(.065,.075,.065,1)
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position=.80
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=(.21,.22,.18,1)
        nt.links.new(noise.outputs["Fac"],ramp.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(ramp.outputs["Color"],bs.inputs["Base Color"])

sc=bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world=bpy.data.worlds.new("SceneWorld")
sc.world.use_nodes=True
nt=sc.world.node_tree
background=nt.nodes.get("Background")
if background is None:
    background=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBackground")
output=nt.nodes.get("World Output")
if output is None:
    output=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputWorld")
nt.links.new(background.outputs["Background"],output.inputs["Surface"])
background.inputs["Color"].default_value=(.64,.70,.76,1)
background.inputs["Strength"].default_value=.32
area_emitter(position=(.22,3.4,2.12),power=420,size=4.6,target=(3.4,4.0,1.0),color=(.88,.94,1.0))
area_emitter(position=(2.2,3.8,2.78),power=100,size=3.7,target=(2.4,4,0),color=(1.0,.94,.81))
set_view(position=(.88,-.42,1.64),target=(2.35,7.25,1.60),lens=24,sensor=32)
sc.camera.data.clip_start=.05
sc.camera.data.clip_end=100
sc.render.resolution_x=384
sc.render.resolution_y=512
sc.render.resolution_percentage=100
sc.view_settings.view_transform='Standard'
sc.view_settings.exposure=0
sc.view_settings.gamma=1
